import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.12

by D. L. Johnson, E. F. Robertson

Let $D0$ denote the class of finite groups of deficiency zero, i.e. having a
presentation $\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$.

a) Does $D0$ contain any 3-generator $p$-group for $p \geq 5$?

c) Do soluble $D0$-groups have bounded derived length?

d) Which non-abelian simple groups can occur as composition factors of $D0$-groups?

Part d) asks for a description rather than a yes/no answer and is not stated here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.12»

/--
A group $G$ has *deficiency zero* if it has a finite presentation
$\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$, i.e. there are a finite set $X$ of generators and a
set $R$ of relators in the free group on $X$ with $|R| = |X|$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to
the presented group $\langle X \mid R \rangle$.
-/
def HasDeficiencyZero (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (X : Type) (_ : Fintype X) (R : Finset (FreeGroup X)),
    Fintype.card X = R.card ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup (R : Set (FreeGroup X)) ≃* G)

/-- The trivial group has deficiency zero: it has the empty presentation
$\langle \varnothing \mid \varnothing \rangle$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasDeficiencyZero_punit : HasDeficiencyZero PUnit := by
  refine ⟨Empty, inferInstance, ∅, by simp, ?_⟩
  haveI : Subsingleton
      (PresentedGroup ((∅ : Finset (FreeGroup Empty)) : Set (FreeGroup Empty))) := by
    constructor
    intro a b
    obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := PresentedGroup.mk_surjective _ a
    obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := PresentedGroup.mk_surjective _ b
    rw [Subsingleton.elim a b]
  haveI : Unique (PresentedGroup ((∅ : Finset (FreeGroup Empty)) : Set (FreeGroup Empty))) :=
    Unique.mk' _
  exact ⟨MulEquiv.ofUnique⟩

/--
Does $D0$ contain any 3-generator $p$-group for $p \geq 5$?

That is, is there a prime $p \geq 5$ and a finite $p$-group $G$ of deficiency zero whose
minimal number of generators $d(G)$ is exactly $3$? The presentation witnessing deficiency
zero need not itself have $3$ generators.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.12».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G),
      p.Prime ∧ 5 ≤ p ∧ IsPGroup p G ∧ Group.rank G = 3 ∧ HasDeficiencyZero G := by
  sorry

/--
Do soluble $D0$-groups have bounded derived length?

That is, is there an $n$ such that every finite soluble group of deficiency zero has
derived length at most $n$, i.e. the $n$-th term of its derived series is trivial?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.12».parts.c : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G],
      IsSolvable G → HasDeficiencyZero G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.12»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. Dropping part d) ('Which non-abelian simple groups can occur as composition factors of D0-groups?') is appropriate: it asks for a description rather than a proposition; I mention it in the module docstring only as not stated.
modeling_decisions: '3-generator p-group' is read as Group.rank G = 3 (minimal number of generators exactly 3), per the decomposition notes; the weaker reading 'generated by 3 elements' would make part a) trivially true (2-generator p-groups of deficiency zero exist for every p).

Relators R are modelled as a Finset (distinct relators) rather than a multiset/list; for finite groups this is equivalent since deficiency > 0 is impossible for a finite group, so a multiset presentation with |X| = |R| already yields a set presentation with |X| = |R|.
Finiteness of G is stated explicitly (Finite G) in both slots rather than folded into HasDeficiencyZero, which is defined for arbitrary groups so it is reusable; D0 = finite ∧ HasDeficiencyZero.
Groups are quantified over Type (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files; every finite group is isomorphic to one in Type, so no generality is lost.
Derived length ≤ n is expressed as derivedSeries G n = ⊥ instead of introducing a derived-length function; this is exactly equivalent since the derived series is antitone.
Group.rank G uses the instance Group.fg_of_finite from [Finite G]; Group.FG is a Prop so the instance choice does not affect the value.

namespace Kourovka.«8.12»

/--
A group $G$ has deficiency zero if it has a finite presentation
$\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$, i.e. there is some $n$ and a set
$R$ of exactly $n$ elements of the free group on $n$ generators such that

def IsDeficiencyZero (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (R : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    R.card = n ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (R : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

/-- The trivial group has deficiency zero, via the empty presentation
$\langle \, \mid \, \rangle$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isDeficiencyZero_unit : IsDeficiencyZero Unit := by
  refine ⟨0, ∅, rfl, ?_⟩
  let R : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0)) := ((∅ : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin 0))) : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0)))
  haveI : Subsingleton (PresentedGroup R) := (PresentedGroup.mk_surjective R).subsingleton
  haveI := Unique.mk' (PresentedGroup R)
  exact ⟨MulEquiv.ofUnique⟩

That is, is there a prime $p \geq 5$ and a finite $p$-group $G$ of deficiency

That is, is there an $n$ such that every finite soluble group of deficiency zero

series is trivial?

    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G],
      IsSolvable G → IsDeficiencyZero G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥ := by
  sorry

namespace Kourovka.«8.12»

/--
A group $G$ has deficiency zero if it has a finite presentation
$\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$, i.e. with the same number of

  haveI := (PresentedGroup.mk_surjective (R : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0)))).subsingleton

  ⟨0, R, rfl, ⟨MulEquiv.ofUnique⟩⟩

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.12

by D. L. Johnson, E. F. Robertson

Let $D0$ be the class of finite groups having a presentation
$\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$. The problem asks whether $D0$
contains a $3$-generator $p$-group for some prime $p \geq 5$, and whether
solvable groups in $D0$ have uniformly bounded derived length.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.12»

/--
Does there exist a prime $p \geq 5$ and a finite $p$-group $G$ whose minimum
number of generators is exactly $3$, such that $G$ has a finite presentation
$\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G),
      p.Prime ∧ 5 ≤ p ∧ IsPGroup p G ∧ Group.rank G = 3 ∧
        ∃ (X : Type) (_ : Fintype X) (R : Finset (FreeGroup X)),
          Fintype.card X = R.card ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (R : Set (FreeGroup X))) := by
  sorry

/--
Is there a uniform bound $n$ such that every finite solvable group $G$ having
a finite presentation $\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$ has derived
length at most $n$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.c : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G),
      IsSolvable G →
        (∃ (X : Type) (_ : Fintype X) (R : Finset (FreeGroup X)),
          Fintype.card X = R.card ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (R : Set (FreeGroup X)))) →
        derivedSeries G n = ⊥ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.12»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.12

by D. L. Johnson, E. F. Robertson

Let $D0$ denote the class of finite groups of deficiency zero, i.e. having a
presentation $\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$.

a) Does $D0$ contain any 3-generator $p$-group for $p \geq 5$?

c) Do soluble $D0$-groups have bounded derived length?

d) Which non-abelian simple groups can occur as composition factors of
$D0$-groups?

Part d) asks for a description rather than a yes/no answer and is not
formalised here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.12»

/--
A group $G$ has *deficiency zero* if it has a presentation
$\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$, i.e. $G$ is isomorphic to
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$ for some $n$ and some set $R$ of $n$
relators (words in the free group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$).
-/
def HasDeficiencyZero (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (R : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    R.card = n ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup (R : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) ≃* G)

/-- The trivial group has deficiency zero: it has the empty presentation
$\langle \varnothing \mid \varnothing \rangle$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasDeficiencyZero_unit : HasDeficiencyZero Unit := by
  refine ⟨0, ∅, Finset.card_empty, ⟨?_⟩⟩
  haveI : Unique (PresentedGroup ((∅ : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin 0))) : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0)))) :=
    ⟨⟨1⟩, fun x => by
      obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := PresentedGroup.mk_surjective _ x
      rw [Subsingleton.elim y 1, map_one]
      rfl⟩
  exact MulEquiv.ofUnique

/--
Does $D0$ contain any 3-generator $p$-group for $p \geq 5$?

That is, is there a prime $p \geq 5$ and a finite $p$-group $G$ of deficiency
zero whose minimal number of generators is exactly $3$? Here "3-generator"
means that $G$ can be generated by $3$ elements but not by fewer, i.e.
`Group.rank G = 3`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.12».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G),
      p.Prime ∧ 5 ≤ p ∧ IsPGroup p G ∧ Group.rank G = 3 ∧ HasDeficiencyZero G := by
  sorry

/--
Do soluble $D0$-groups have bounded derived length?

That is, is there an $n$ such that every finite soluble group of deficiency
zero has derived length at most $n$? A group $G$ has derived length at most
$n$ exactly when the $n$-th term $G^{(n)}$ of its derived series is trivial.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.12».parts.c : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] [IsSolvable G],
      HasDeficiencyZero G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.12»

modeling_decisions: Relators are counted as a set (Finset with card exactly n), matching the notebook's |X| = |R| literally. Counting with multiplicity (Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)) would be equivalent for finite groups, since a finite group has no presentation with fewer relators than generators, and a set of relators can always be padded with distinct powers of a nontrivial relator.
